title: FEC Advisory Opinion 2025-07: 4 Libertarian State Committees
text:
FEDERAL ELECTION COMMISSION
WASHINGTON, D.C.
April 30, 2025
ADVISORY OPINION 2025-07
Lorenzo Holloway, Esq.
Holloway Law Office, LLC
National Harbor
6710 Oxon Hill Rd. Suite 210
Oxon Hill, MD 20745
Dear Mr. Holloway:
We are responding to your request on behalf of the Libertarian Party of Idaho, the
Libertarian Party of Maine, Inc., the Libertarian Party of Maryland, and the Libertarian Party of
Vermont (the “Requestors”) regarding their status as state committees of a political party under
the Federal Election Campaign Act, 52 U.S.C. §§ 30101-45 (the “Act”), and Commission
regulations. The Commission concludes that the Requestors qualify as state committees of a
political party.
Background
The facts presented in this advisory opinion are based on your advisory opinion request
received on April 4, 2025, public disclosure reports filed with the Commission, and other
publicly available information.
In 1976, the Commission recognized the Libertarian National Committee, Inc. (“LNC”)
as the national committee of the Libertarian National Party.1 The LNC’s chair, Mr. Steven
Nekhaila, has confirmed by letter that the Requestors “are officially chartered affiliates of the
[LNC].”2

the Libertarian Party of Idaho were each designated as the state committee of the LNC. Advisory Opinion 2016-14

Question Presented
Do the Requestors qualify as state committees of a political party within the meaning of
the Act and Commission regulations?
Legal Analysis
Yes, the Requestors qualify as state committees of a political party within the meaning of
the Act and Commission regulations.
Whether a state party organization qualifies as a state committee of a national political
party turns on three elements: (1) the national organization affiliated with the state party
organization must itself be a “political party”9; (2) the state party organization must be part of the
official structure of the national party; and (3) the state party organization must be responsible
for the day-to-day operation of the national party at the state level.10 The Commission addresses
each of these elements in turn.
(1) Qualification of Libertarian National Party as Political Party
The national party, the Libertarian National Party, must qualify as a “political party”
under the Act and Commission regulations, and the Commission has previously determined that
it does.11 The Commission is not aware of any factual changes that would alter that
determination.
(2) Status of the Requestor as Part of the Official Structure of Party
To determine whether a state party organization is part of the official structure of a
national party, the Commission evaluates documentation from the national party.12 The letter

9 A “political party” is an “association, committee, or organization which nominates a candidate for election
to any Federal office whose name appears on the election ballot as the candidate of such association, committee, or
organization.” 52 U.S.C. § 30101(16); 11 C.F.R. § 100.15. An individual is a candidate if the individual or his or
her authorized committee has received contributions aggregating in excess of $5,000 or made expenditures
aggregating in excess of $5,000. See 52 U.S.C. § 30101(2); 11 C.F.R. § 100.3(a)(1).
10 See, e.g., Advisory Opinion 2025-02 (Democratic Party of Puerto Rico); Advisory Opinion 2024-15

from the LNC’s Chair, Mr. Steven Nekhaila, confirms that the Requestors are part of the official
structure of the Libertarian National Party.13
(3) Responsibility of the Requestor for Day-to-Day Operation of the Party at the State
Level
To determine whether a state party organization is responsible for the day-to-day
operations of a national party at the state level, the Commission considers: (a) whether the state
organization has placed a federal candidate on the ballot (thereby qualifying as a “political party”
under 52 U.S.C. § 30101(16)); and (b) whether the bylaws or other governing documents of the
state party organization indicate activity commensurate with the day-to-day functions and
operations of a political party at the state level.14
(a) Candidate on the Ballot
The Requestors placed the Libertarian National Party’s nominee for President, Chase
Oliver, on the 2024 general election ballot in their respective states.15 Chase Oliver’s campaign
committee received contributions or made expenditures in excess of $5,000 according to public
disclosure reports filed with the Commission,16 therefore satisfying the Act’s definition of a
“candidate.”17 The Requestors thus placed a federal candidate on the ballot.
(b) Day-To-Day Functions and Operations
In addition to gaining ballot access for a candidate for federal office, the Requestors must
show — in their bylaws, constitution, or other governing documents — that they are responsible
for activity commensurate with the day-to-day functions and operations of a national political
party at the state level.18
Here, the Requestors’ respective bylaws indicate that they engage in various political
party activities that the Commission has found sufficient to qualify an organization for state-
committee status.19 The Requestors’ bylaws indicate that they each engage in various political

party activities in their respective states.20 These activities include promoting libertarian
principles,21 holding and overseeing state conventions, 22 sending delegates to the Libertarian
National Party’s national convention,23 and nominating and supporting candidates for public
office in their respective states.24 The bylaws also provide for the election of officers for their
respective state committees, and the selection of officers for their respective local committees.25
Based on these activities, the Requestors satisfy the requirement of being responsible for the day-
to-day operation of the Libertarian National Party at the state level pursuant to 52 U.S.C.
§ 30101(15) and 11 C.F.R. § 100.14(a).
Conclusion
The Commission concludes that the Requestors qualify as state committees of a political
party under the Act and Commission regulations because: (1) the Party qualifies as a political
party; (2) the Requestors are part of the official structure of the Party; and (3) the Requestors are
responsible for the day-to-day operation of the Party at the state level.
This response constitutes an advisory opinion concerning the application of the Act and
Commission regulations to the specific transaction or activity set forth in your request.26 The
Commission emphasizes that, if there is a change in any of the facts or assumptions presented,
and such facts or assumptions are material to a conclusion presented in this advisory opinion,
then the Requestor may not rely on that conclusion as support for its proposed activity. Any
person involved in any specific transaction or activity which is indistinguishable in all its
bylaws show that is endorses national party’s principles, sends delegates to national convention, and establishes
requirements for committee elections, among other activities); Advisory Opinion 2024-15 (United Libertarians of
Massachusetts) at 4-5 (concluding that requestor’s responsibilities to promote national party principles, endorse
candidates for public office, send delegates to the party’s national convention, and recognize local affiliates, among
other duties detailed in bylaws, demonstrated requestor’s responsibility for day-to-day functions and operations of
national party at state level); Advisory Opinion 2023-12 (Democratic Party of the Northern Mariana Islands) at 4-5
(concluding that requestor’s responsibilities to nominate candidates for state and federal offices, elect delegates to
national party’s national convention, establish requirements for election of committees, among other duties detailed
in bylaws, demonstrated requestor’s responsibility for day-to-day functions and operations of national party to
qualify for state committee status); Advisory Opinion 2019-03 (DC Libertarian Party) at 4-5 (finding that
requestor’s political party activities described in bylaws, including recruiting, nominating and training candidates for
partisan public office, sending delegates to party’s national convention, managing District of Columbia party
conventions, among other duties, established requestor’s responsibility for day-to-day operation of national party at
state level to qualify for state committee status).
